terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A parked vehicle prop: an exterior shell with no interior geometry, since a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside and the glazing is authored as a tinted, mostly opaque pane. The wheels are the mechanisms: each is a named pivot on its axle. Nothing else moves and nothing attaches, so there are no sockets. A Bangkok tuk-tuk. The plate shows a glossy green scooter nose with a yellow centre band, a chrome-ringed headlamp and a slot grille in it, a green headstock nacelle under chrome bars with one mirror on the left, a deep green front mudguard with a chrome bead, a dark rubber floor mat with a chrome edge rail, a green half door in a chrome frame whose rear leg hooks down as an armrest, a chrome pillar from the door's rear-top corner to the roof lip, a green cabin tub with a yellow belt stripe under a chrome belt rail, a broad green C-pillar whose opening edge is chrome-trimmed up and along the roof lip, a domed green canopy, a dark green vinyl bench with a back, a green tube basket on the tail with the exhaust below it, one front wheel and two rear wheels on pressed-steel rims.

reasoning: The identity is the three-part layout read off the proxy depth maps and the plate crops: a scooter nose (single front wheel under a deep fender, a concave leg shield with the yellow centre band, lamp and slot grille, a headstock nacelle under the bars) at z +0.76..+1.45, an open rubber-matted floor from z +0.90 back to the cabin, and a passenger cabin whose domed roof runs from a lip at z +0.84 back into an ENCLOSED rear quarter -- 1.90 @ -0.72, 1.80 @ -1.00, 1.57 @ -1.13 -- and a vertical tail at z -1.16.

Four materials: gloss paint (green, yellow band and stripe as vertex colours, one dust canvas), a white vertex-coloured trim (chrome rails, lamp, exhaust, window pane, tail lamps, sump), rubber for the three pressed-steel wheels, and a soft material for the bench and mat with a grime canvas.
One repetition system: three pressed-steel wheels off one 19-point lathe, each a named pivot on its axle.
Action readiness is the wheels: three hinge pivots, convex collider, not breakable. Steering is not articulated because the fork, bars and front wheel live in three different draw calls.

specDepthDecision.rationale: An auto rickshaw is legible by its openness -- a half door and a chrome pillar at the front of the cabin, an open side down to the belt, a broad green C-pillar carrying a roof that cantilevers 1.1 m forward over the driver -- so the shell is ONE C-section extrusion (roof band, tail wall, floor pan) with the cabin between its arms, the sides are quarter-panel strips, and the turntable sees the backdrop through the cabin from every side: that is the vehicle, not a hole in the model.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: The cabin is open-sided and the turntable gate's enclosed-background signal fires on the backdrop seen through it from every azimuth. That is real open air; --allow-holes is set on the _holecc measurement.

The rear window is inferred from the proxy's rear elevation (a 0.6 m opening over y 1.3-1.65); the plate cannot see the tail. Built as a pale glazed panel in a chrome surround, 0.60 x 0.28 m, confidence 0.6.
No driver's saddle: the plate and the proxy both show an empty matted floor between the leg shield and the half door, and the floor is built as they show it.
The body is built 1.20 m wide over a 1.28 m rear track (proxy 1.17 / 1.30) against a declared 1.40: the declaration was a list-time estimate and the proxy is the measurement.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 1.40 x 1.95 x 2.90 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4800 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=4 materials, <=8 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus one named pivot per wheel (3); zero sockets; convex collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

silhouette.description: Front wheel 0.54 m at z +1.18 under a fender arc from 37 to 168 degrees; leg shield front face bellying to z 1.00 at y 0.75, raking back to the cowl top at (0.76-0.82, 1.21); nacelle to 1.30 m leaning 23 degrees; bars at 1.21 m; floor top 0.34 m from z +0.905 to the tail; half door z +0.11..-0.29 at 0.42-0.98 m; front pillar at z -0.27; belt 0.70-0.72 m; C-pillar opening edge from (-0.82, 0.72) up to the roof at (-0.42, 1.92); roof lip z +0.858 at 1.835 m, crown 1.925 + 0.03 across the width, rear arc to a vertical tail at z -1.16 from 1.45 down to 0.28; rear wheels 0.54 m at z -0.69 on a 1.16 m track; basket 0.63-1.03 m to z -1.43.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -0.64..+0.64 at the rear wheels and -0.60..+0.60 at the body; y 0.00 to 1.95 at the roof crown; z -1.44..+1.46 basket to fender tip, +Z forward. The Meshy proxy normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.662 : 0.449, i.e. 2.90 x 1.92 x 1.30 m at the declared length: height within 2 percent of the registry, width 7 percent under it (the proxy reads the body at 1.17 and the rear track at 1.30), so the body is built to the proxy and the declared 1.40 is the tolerance ceiling. Every longitudinal station is read off the side depth map (scratch/tuk-tuk/_ev/stations.py) in real metres.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.662 : 0.449 and agrees with the registry on height. Its side depth map (scratch/tuk-tuk/_ev/side.pgm, read column by column in real metres) gives the front wheel z +0.91..+1.45, the shield front at z ~1.00 from y 0.35 to 0.85 raking back to (0.84, 1.21), bars 1.12-1.22, the canopy lip at z +0.84 (1.83-1.87) with its top at 1.92, the roof curving DOWN into an enclosed rear quarter (1.90 @ -0.72, 1.85 @ -0.93, 1.80 @ -1.00, 1.57 @ -1.13), a vertical tail at -1.16 to 0.35, and the basket 0.61-1.03 to -1.42; the rear elevation gives the body 1.17 wide, the track 1.30 and a 0.6 m rear window. The proxy puts the front pillar at z +0.07; the plate (crop-door.png) puts it at the half-door's rear-top corner, and the plate wins for the arrangement.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.6: the tail wall, its 0.6 m window and the tail lamps are built from the proxy's rear elevation and to type.

buildPasses.goal: Build the component hierarchy implied by the pre-spec complexity assessment.
acceptance: Macro, meso, and repeated structures meet qualityContract.minimumSpecDepth.
Parent-child relations, joints, seams, sockets, and contact points are explicit.
Every attached child appendage/connector has parentSocket, localStart/localEnd, contactType, embedDepth or overlap, and gapTolerance.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Refine shape, deformation, bevels, tapers, curves, asymmetry, and visible local geometry.
acceptance: Important visible forms are represented in component geometryDescriptor, deformations, localFeatures, or repetitionSystems.
Endpoint-based child parts are rooted at their attachment sockets and do not visibly float away from parents.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump/displacement, AO, dirt, stains, chips, grain, moss, scratches, and wear.
acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.
A grazing-angle close-up proves that normal/height detail breaks highlights naturally and does not read as smooth plastic.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 1.28 x 1.95 x 2.90 m against a declared 1.40 x 1.95 x 2.90; the proxy reads the body at 1.17 and the rear track at 1.30 (1 : 0.662 : 0.449), so the width is built to the measurement and the declaration is the tolerance ceiling. Every longitudinal station is read off the side depth map in real metres (scratch/tuk-tuk/_ev/stations.py).
featureReviews.notes: The deleted build was a flat lens canopy on chrome sticks over a box tub, with a slab nose and disc wheels. featureReviews.evidence: Three instanced pressed-steel wheels: hub cap, dished centre, vent ring, rim lip and a tread whose lugs alternate two tones per segment, 19 points at 12 segments. Tyre held on chroma at #3a3226; hub #9a958c measured off the plate's front wheel.
featureReviews.notes: 12 segments is the floor for a 0.54 m wheel; 14 cost 228 triangles across the three instances for no visible gain at prop distance.

featureReviews.evidence: One C-section shell (roof band with a 9 cm shoulder fillet, a 3 cm cross-width crown and 28/22 cm plan roundings, tail wall, floor pan), quarter-panel strips with the arch cut, a half door in a chrome frame whose rear leg hooks down as an armrest, a chrome pillar from the door's rear-top corner to the roof lip, a broad C-pillar with the chrome rail running up its opening edge and round the roof lip, bench with a leaning back, mat, rear window, green tube basket.
featureReviews.notes: Three faults came out of the renders rather than any gate. The yellow belt stripe vanished into the panel: first because the arch flare stood over it (arch dropped to hub height, stripe raised under the belt), then because a plan rounding projects only the vertices inside its corner zone, so a strip's single earcut cap triangulation ran from an unprojected front vertex to a projected tail vertex and tilted the whole face 6 cm inward -- the shell's floor edge was dragged 4 cm inside the panels the same way. Fixed with a vertex at every tangent station and by cutting the panel and stripe into 6-8 cm slices through the corner. The roof-lip rail also rode 1.5 cm above the lip at the front and read as a pale sliver.

featureReviews.evidence: Leg shield tumbled 32% to the cowl top and plan-rounded r 0.10, bellying to z 1.00 at y 0.75 off the depth map; yellow centre band 12 mm proud with a tilted chrome-bezel lamp buried 4 cm into the shield and three grille slots; headstock nacelle lathe leaning 23 degrees; bars, black grips, left mirror; fender hugging the tyre 37-168 degrees with chrome beads; chrome edge trim down both shield sides continuing into the floor rail.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's shield is broader and more concave than a 0.50 m sweep can carry without a second profile; the band and lamp placement are read off crop-nose.png.

featureReviews.notes: Stripe visible end to end on the 090/270 frames and wrapping to the tail on 180.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.90. 4,514/4,800 triangles (asset ceiling raised from 4,000 with the arithmetic in notes), 4/4 draw calls, 4/4 materials, 4/8 unique geometries, two 256 px canvases at 0.7 MB, factory 74 ms. Turntable: enclosed background is the open cabin, allowed on measurement.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Three components and one repetition system: 4 of 4.

materials.note: paint, trim, rubber and soft, every one white with vertex colours: 4 of 4.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 4,514 of 4,800 (asset ceiling; the class default 4,000 was set against the deleted 3,244-triangle slab build): three 12-segment 19-point wheels are 1,368, the shell, panels and corner slices ~1,600, the chrome work ~1,400.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Side-profile extrusions and strips for the shell, quarter panels, stripe, shield, band and fender; lathes for the nacelle, lamp and wheels; polyline tubes for every chrome and basket part; boxes for doors, wings, bench, mat, lamps.
One InstancedMesh carries all three wheels. No per-instance colour.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Every material is declared textureless. One 256 px dust canvas on the paint and one on the soft material: 0.7 MB of texture VRAM, factory 74 ms.

risks.description: The turntable gate flags the backdrop through the open cabin at every azimuth.
risks.mitigation: Real open air; --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement.

risks.description: The derived compound boxes the rounded, cantilevered roof, so 12% of the footprint stands over a step height above the real surface at the roof corners.
risks.mitigation: Under the 15% gate; a hand compound with a narrower roof box is the follow-up if a level walks on it.

risks.description: The rear window is inferred from the proxy, not seen on the plate.
risks.mitigation: Recorded as an assumption at confidence 0.6.
